title: 古从军行
titleEn: An Old Song of Marching to War
author: 李颀
intro: A Tang poet borrows a Han-dynasty war to protest the wars of his own day: soldiers freeze and die in the desert year after year, and all the empire gets in return is grapes.
analysis: “从军行”是乐府旧题，前面加个“古”字，表面写汉朝的事，其实是借古讽今，批评唐朝皇帝不断开边打仗。前四句写军中的一天：白天登山看烽火，黄昏到河边饮马，夜里只听见巡夜的刁斗声和像汉朝远嫁公主那样哀怨的琵琶。中间四句写环境：万里荒野没有城郭，大雪连着沙漠，连大雁和本地胡人都在哀鸣落泪，更不用说远来的士兵。最后四句是全诗的重点：听说玉门关被挡住，不许回家，只能拼命跟着将军继续打；年年有人战死埋在荒野，换来的只是葡萄运进皇宫。用这么大的代价和这么小的收获作对比，讽刺不说破却很尖锐。
analysisEn: “Marching to War” was an old folk-song title; adding 古 (“old”) lets Li Qi set the poem in the Han dynasty while really aiming at the Tang emperors of his own time, who kept pushing the frontier outward. This trick of criticising the present through the past is very common in Chinese poetry. The first four lines give a soldier’s day: watching for beacon fires by day, watering horses at dusk, and at night hearing only the watchman’s copper pot and a pipa as mournful as the one played by a Han princess married off to a nomad king. The middle four lines paint the land: endless clouds, no towns, snow running into the desert. Even the wild geese cry, and even the soldiers born out here weep — so imagine the men from far away. The last four lines carry the point. In Han times the emperor once closed the Jade Gate so a failing army could not come home; these men, too, can only risk their lives and press on. Every year more bones are buried in the waste, and what reaches the capital? Grapes. Setting that huge cost against that tiny prize is the poem’s quiet, sharp protest.
background: Li Qi (c. 690–c. 751) was a minor official in the High Tang, admired for his frontier poems and his friendships with Daoist recluses. This poem is usually read as a protest against Emperor Xuanzong’s expensive campaigns in the west, disguised as a story about Emperor Wu of Han.
pronunciation: 饮马 yìn mǎ（让马喝水，不读 yǐn）；傍 bàng（靠近）；刁斗 diāo dǒu；城郭 guō；将 jiāng（拿）；轻车 chē（旧读 jū，今按 chē）。雨雪纷纷：“雨”作动词“下”，传统读 yù；此处参照统编教材《采薇》“雨雪霏霏”的注音采用 yù，也有人按今音读 yǔ。机器朗读“饮马”“雨雪”易读错，已在“朗读用字”列替换同音字，音频需人工听验。
version: 采用通行的《唐诗三百首》文本。“野云万里无城郭”一作“野营万里无城郭”；“蒲桃”即“葡萄”，古书多写作“蒲桃”或“蒲萄”，有的选本直接写“葡萄”。“公主琵琶”用汉代乌孙公主远嫁、马上弹琵琶的传说。

lines.py: bái rì dēng shān wàng fēng huǒ
lines.lit: In daylight we climb the hills to watch for beacon fires;
lines.en: By day we climb the ridge to watch for signal fires;

lines.py: huáng hūn yìn mǎ bàng jiāo hé
lines.lit: at dusk we water our horses beside the Jiao River.
lines.en: at dusk we lead the horses down to drink at the Jiao River.

lines.py: xíng rén diāo dǒu fēng shā àn
lines.lit: The marchers’ watch-pots — wind and sand are dark;
lines.en: Through the dark of blowing sand, the night watch beats its copper pot,

lines.py: gōng zhǔ pí pá yōu yuàn duō
lines.lit: the princess’s pipa — so much hidden grief.
lines.en: and a pipa, like the exiled princess’s, plays its sorrow.

lines.py: yě yún wàn lǐ wú chéng guō
lines.lit: Wild clouds for ten thousand li, no city walls;
lines.en: Wild clouds for a thousand miles, and not one walled town;

lines.py: yù xuě fēn fēn lián dà mò
lines.lit: it snows thick and fast, joining the great desert.
lines.en: the snow keeps falling, on and on into the desert.

lines.py: hú yàn āi míng yè yè fēi
lines.lit: The northern geese cry sadly, flying night after night;
lines.en: Wild geese of the steppe fly crying, night after night,

lines.py: hú ér yǎn lèi shuāng shuāng luò
lines.lit: the nomad soldiers’ tears fall in pairs.
lines.en: and even the men born out here are weeping.

lines.py: wén dào yù mén yóu bèi zhē
lines.lit: I hear the Jade Gate is still blocked;
lines.en: We hear the Jade Gate is still barred against us —

lines.py: yīng jiāng xìng mìng zhú qīng chē
lines.lit: we must take our lives and follow the Light-Chariot general.
lines.en: so we must stake our lives and follow the general on.

lines.py: nián nián zhàn gǔ mái huāng wài
lines.lit: Year after year, war bones are buried beyond the wilds;
lines.en: Year after year, soldiers’ bones are buried in the waste,

lines.py: kōng jiàn pú táo rù hàn jiā
lines.lit: in vain we see grapes enter the house of Han.
lines.en: and all there is to show for it: grapes, carried home to the emperor.

words.en: beacon fire; signal fire on the frontier
words.note: 古代边境报警用的火，现代汉语“烽火”多指战火。
“饮”读 yìn，是“让……喝”；现代汉语说“饮牲口”，较少用。
现代汉语“依山傍水”“傍晚”还用。

words.en: the Jiao River (near today’s Turpan, Xinjiang)
words.note: 古地名，今新疆吐鲁番附近还有交河故城。

words.en: a copper pot used for cooking by day and beaten as a watch-gong at night
words.note: 古代军中用具，现代已不用。
书面语，现代汉语仍用，如“幽怨的眼神”。
“城”是内城，“郭”是外城；现代汉语说“城市”“城镇”。
“雨”作动词，意思是“下”；现代汉语说“下雪”。

words.en: the northern and western nomad peoples; foreign
words.note: 古代称北方、西方民族；今天“胡萝卜”“胡琴”的“胡”就是这个来源。
古义，“道”是“说”；现代汉语说“听说”。

words.en: the Jade Gate Pass, the western gateway of the empire
words.note: 今甘肃玉门关遗址仍在。

words.en: must take…; have no choice but to…
light chariots; here the general leading them
words.note: 汉代有“轻车将军”的官名，这里代指带兵的将领。
即“葡萄”，汉代从西域传入；现代汉语只写“葡萄”。
唐诗里常用“汉”代指唐朝。

imagery.name: 烽火
imagery.zh: 白天登山就是为了看烽火，写出边境随时会有战争的紧张。
imagery.en: The soldiers climb the hills just to watch for beacon fires — war could break out at any moment.

imagery.name: 琵琶
imagery.zh: 琵琶声让人想起汉代远嫁西域的公主，弹出的全是离乡的哀怨。
imagery.en: The pipa recalls the Han princess sent to marry a nomad king; its music is all homesick grief.

imagery.name: 雁
imagery.zh: 胡雁夜夜哀鸣着飞过，连鸟都觉得这里太苦，更衬出士兵回不了家。
imagery.en: Geese fly over crying every night; even birds find this land harsh — and unlike them, the soldiers cannot leave.
